summary: A 20-foot steel fire tower on Sunset Peak in the Angeles National Forest, built in 1927 and taken down in 1974-75; only footings and a foundation remain.

facts.design: 20-ft steel tower with a cab (sources differ: L-4 or BC-301 per the register; 14 by 14 ft wood cab per Angeles Adventures)
facts.status_note: Tower and cab removed in 1974-75 and reportedly taken to the Ontario air tanker base; footings and a house foundation remain.

access.note: Reached on foot by a fire road and trail from Cow Canyon Saddle on Glendora Ridge Road; check Angeles National Forest for closures before going.

visit.trail_note: Trailhead at Cow Canyon Saddle; parking is roadside only; HikingGuy lists the hike at 7.5 miles.

events.note: March 1915 newspaper: a 50-foot steel tower planned for the crest; not the 20-foot tower later built
Lookout built on Sunset Peak to replace the Old Baldy (Lookout Mountain) station; 20-foot steel tower
Charles E. Horn and his wife stationed at the lookout; a 1928 item says Horn had been there two years
Lightning and then fire destroyed the cabin; the steel tower survived and the lookout was quickly rebuilt
Winter motorway built; July 1933 item says an automobile was used that summer in place of the pack trains (Angeles Adventures dates the first motor supply run to 1932)
San Antonio Fire threatened the lookout from both sides; lookout Sherman Foster stayed at his post and warned the WPA camp foreman
1960s photo caption: F.A. Vickery was possibly the last lookout (year approximate)
Deactivated because smog pollution obstructed visibility
Cab and tower reportedly disassembled and transported to the Ontario Air Tanker Base in 1974 or 75
Angeles Adventures gives the span as 1927-1975 and lists the structure as demolished

corrections.why: 15.2 m is 50 feet, the height in the March 1915 plan; the register and Angeles Adventures both give the built tower as 20 feet

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1915 plan said 50 feet; the 1927 item, the register and Angeles Adventures say 20 feet for the built tower
The 1927 item says a new tower was to replace the Old Baldy station; Angeles Adventures says the old tower was moved. Both point to 1927
The register thinks the cab was an L-4 or BC-301 type; Angeles Adventures gives a 14 by 14 foot wood cab
The register gives removal in 1974 and transport to Ontario in 1974 or 75; Angeles Adventures gives 1975 and says demolished
Angeles Adventures dates the first motor supply run to 1932; the July 1933 item describes an automobile replacing the pack trains that summer after a winter motorway was built

notes_for_editor: Built 1927 is consistent across the three history sources. The 1928 Horn item says he had been stationed there for two years, which would predate the 1927 build; the story does not use this. Removal year and fate differ (register 1974 transported; Angeles Adventures 1975 demolished). The HikingGuy page mentions the 2021 Antonio Fire along the trail, not the summit. A 2024 fire was seen only in a search snippet and is not used. No page describing the current site condition was read beyond the register's 2013 photo captions. The brief's height_m of 15.2 appears to come from the 1915 50-foot plan.
